text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.1% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tension. Iran's escalation of tanker attacks in the Persian Gulf, combined with reports that the Trump administration is preparing large-scale military operations against Iran, pushed crude prices sharply higher—world oil climbed to $125.44 per barrel. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly improve earnings on both the exploration and production side and, in some cases, the refining margin.

The move also reflects a broader wave of energy sector strength tied to supply disruption fears. A hurricane threatening U.S. Gulf production, tanker shortages driving shipping costs to 10 times pre-war levels, and political pressure around fuel prices all point to a tightening global energy market—conditions that historically favor large oil producers with diversified operations.
